Site: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/space.rs:416

Currently returns SetError::Forbidden with message 'Role, member, and channel mutations are not yet implemented' for structural patches on Space objects.

Pairs with JMAP-g7wu.2's chat-client task for Space/set sub-ops — the client-side wrapper expects this server-side handler to land.
notes:
[2026-05-10 do-beads triage — sizing assessment]

After reading draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 \xc2\xa7Space/set (lines 1072-1129), this bead's scope is far too large for a single do-beads claim. Implementation requires:

  1. Backend trait extension — either 12+ new ChatBackend methods (add_space_role, remove_space_role, update_space_role, add_space_member, remove_space_member, update_space_member, add_space_channel, remove_space_channel, update_space_channel, add_space_category, remove_space_category, update_space_category) OR one generic apply_space_patch method with a discriminator enum. Design decision; not yet locked.
  2. Permission-check enforcement (manage_space, manage_roles, manage_members, manage_channels — see spec lines 1093, 1096, 1102, 1105, 1108, 1111, 1114, 1117, 1120, 1123, 1126, 1129).
  3. Role-hierarchy enforcement: members may only add/modify roles whose 'position' is strictly less than their own highest-position role (lines 1096, 1102).
  4. Cascading semantics:
     - removeRoles: members holding only removed roles demoted to @everyone (line 1099).
     - removeChannels: cascades to all Messages in those channels (line 1117).
     - removeCategories: channels move to uncategorizedChannelIds (line 1126).
  5. Count limits: maxRolesPerSpace, maxSpaceMembers, maxChannelsPerSpace, maxCategoriesPerSpace.
  6. ULID assignment for new roles/categories/channels.
  7. Atomicity: spec implies single-transaction semantics for each patch.
  8. Tests for all 12 mutation keys plus permission/error/edge cases.

Realistic estimate: 800-1500 LOC across chat-server + chat-types backend.rs + tests + (probably) a feature on the MemoryBackend reference impl in tests/common. Multiple focused sessions.

[Sequencing question for human, filed per workspace AGENTS.md 'Turn questions into beads' rule]

Recommended decomposition before any claim:

  Option A: convert this bead to an epic with one child per mutation family:
    .a addRoles/removeRoles/updateRoles
    .b addMembers/removeMembers/updateMembers
    .c addChannels/removeChannels/updateChannels
    .d addCategories/removeCategories/updateCategories
    .e Backend trait shape decision (associated-type vs generic; one big method vs 12 small ones)
    .e MUST land first because .a-.d depend on the trait shape.

  Option B: keep this bead atomic, scope to 'land all 12 mutations in a single PR'.

  Option C: pre-decision land the backend trait shape (.e) as its own bead, then file four follow-up sibling beads.

Recommendation: option C — single design-decision bead for backend trait shape, then four per-family beads.

This bead is now labeled 'human' to keep the do-beads loop from spinning on it.
De-labeling human (2026-05-11, Mark): umbrella epic for chat Space/set work. The decomposition decision and the architectural identity-seam decision are both complete. All actionable children (.3, .6, .8, .10, .11) carry their own labels/state. Removing human; epic remains open until all children close.
